extracted.intended_audience: research assistants/coders and researchers coding/analyzing notice-and-comment public comments for the Judge‑Lord dissertation (and similar rulemaking datasets)
extracted.subtask_description: A coding handbook for classifying and summarizing public comments submitted to agency rulemakings, including variables for comment types, organizational metadata, asks, outcomes, agency responses, and rule-level measures of regulatory stringency and coalitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: comment_type classification
rubrics_metrics.description: "comment_type" values and definitions: 'org' (organization), 'elected' (individual elected official), 'individual' (writing in personal capacity, not on behalf of an organization or office and not part of an organized petition-like campaign), 'corp campaign' (form letter used by many businesses), 'mass' (petition-like campaign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mass subtypes: 'mass;grassroots' = individuals who genuinely care; 'mass;astroturf' = campaigns intended to create a deceptive appearance of public support (often paid, individuals deceived or incentivized, may include fake names); 'mass;corp campaign' = many businesses mobilized. Use semicolons to add subtype labels. If unsure whether mass is astroturf vs grassroots, ask "why are these people supporting this company/industry?" — if it seems suspicious, mark astroturf.

rubrics_metrics.name: org_name (for comment_type = 'org')
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the organization. This column may be auto-filled; coders must revise to the clearest, standardized, and unique version of the organization’s name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one org signed, try to pick the main organizer (e.g., whose letterhead is used). If unclear, choose an org seen before to improve linking to lobbying coalitions; if still unclear, use the first signatory. When more than one org signed, add "; coalition" to the end of whatever org_type codes you give it.

rubrics_metrics.name: org_type and org_type subcodes (for comment_type = 'org')
rubrics_metrics.description: Code the type of organization: 'corp'/'corp group'/'gov'/'ngo'/etc. Use semicolons to indicate subtypes (e.g., 'ngo;advocacy').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 'corp' = individual business (add subtypes like 'corp;small business', 'corp;coop', 'corp;law firm'); 'corp group' = business interests/trade association; 'gov' = government interests with subtypes ('gov;state','gov;local','gov;federal','gov;tribal','gov;regional','gov;foreign') and list states for multi-state actors; 'ngo' = non-business and non-government interests. Examples of ngo subtypes: 'ngo;advocacy', 'ngo;legal', 'ngo;professional', 'ngo;philanthropy', 'ngo;union', 'ngo;credit union', 'ngo;pressure group', 'ngo;membership organization', 'ngo;university', 'ngo;thinktank', 'ngo;church'. Use semicolons to separate multiple tags. Notes: some 501(c)(3)s may act as industry associations (code as 'corp group'); Chamber of Commerce may be coded according to how it functions (private interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: ask / ask1 / ask2 / ask3 (comment-level asks)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'ask' = the text of the comment (e.g., a sentence) that best captures the overall ask. 'ask1','ask2','ask3' = the comment's top three specific asks or objections (if up to three).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a comment responds to several issues, select the main ask from each of the top three issues (not just the first three mentioned). Put yourself in the organization's shoes and decide which issues are most important given their mission/members. Identify the clearest statements of their top 3 aims and include surrounding on-topic text. If only a general sentiment exists, ask1 can repeat the same ask and leave ask2/ask3 blank. If asks express different intensities (e.g., 'opposes' vs 'strongly opposes'), let intensity guide which issues are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: success / success1 / success2 / success3 (coding outcome of asks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code whether the final rule ended up where requested for the corresponding ask(s): values: '2', '1', '0', '-1', '-2'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaning: '2' = overall, the final rule ended up mostly where requested; '1' = ended somewhat close to that requested; '0' = no adverse changes but no requests met, or request moot (or if they requested publication as-is and it was published as-is, that is a 2); '-1' = rule ended somewhat different/opposite than requested; '-2' = rule ended significantly different/opposite than requested. Note: '-1' and '-2' can include rules published without requested changes or withdrawn when group preferred otherwise. Focus on changes from the proposed to the final rule. Example: if org wanted rule strengthened and it was published as-is, code 0. If mixed asks, choose 0 or 1 depending on importance of demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: success_certainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of coder certainty about the success coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use '1' = fairly certain (may also be left blank), '2' = unsure, '3' = totally unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: response (agency response text and final_url)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paste the text of the agency’s response to the comment. final_url contains the link to the final rule (where agencies often respond).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the federal register final rule text to extract agency replies. Record the specific phrases used by the agency that map to accept/compromise/concession/reject and other response categories (see A.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: elected comment coding (comment_type = 'elected')
rubrics_metrics.description: Coding rules when comment_type = 'elected': only for individual elected officials writing personally (not when writing on behalf of a state government).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: org_name (or elected_name) = official's full name. If more than one official, record the first one except for US House/Senate (record all names separated by ';'). org_type (or elected_type) = official's position. For U.S. Senators/Representatives use 'Chamber-[STATE ABBREV]' (e.g., 'Senate-WI', 'House-NY'). For state reps, start with state (e.g., 'Wisconsin Assembly District 4'). Make sure to code coalition and coalition_type. Code ask and success variables as described for 'org'.

rubrics_metrics.name: mass comment coding (comment_type = 'mass')
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for coding mass comment campaigns: code org_name and org_type as the organization mobilizing the campaign (if known); every mass comment must be assigned a coalition and coalition_type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave ask, success, and response columns blank for mass comments. Check that number_of_comments_received matches comments/signatures submitted; if not, correct it. If sheet has a transparency column, code whether campaign was transparent about its 'sponsor', 'signers', 'both', or 'neither' (otherwise record transparency in notes). Record platform(s) used to generate comments (e.g., 'VoterVoice','Care2','SalesForce') in platform column or notes. If sheet has a fraud column, record any indication of fraud (e.g., 'DMARC validation failed'); otherwise record evidence of fraud in notes. Be alert to astroturf: lack of contact info, misleading org names, or disguised sponsor are signs of low transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: individual comment coding (comment_type = 'individual')
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for coding individual comments: only code position, coalition, coalition_type if immediately obvious; 'individual' is for personal-capacity comments (not on behalf of a group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an individual comment is technical and clearly from a group member (e.g., a professor), try to code coalition; otherwise record comment_type as 'individual' and move on. Leave org_name, org_type, ask, and success blank unless the individual's org also submitted comments on behalf of the org; then org_name can help identify coalition but is not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: accept / compromise / concession / reject phrase coding (A.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify text in agency responses that map to: accept_phrases (granting request), compromise_phrases (partial agreement on main dimension), concession_phrases (neither agreement nor disagreement — off main dimension, includes delays), reject_phrases (indicating rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: accept, compromise, concession, and reject are mutually exclusive. When more than one type applies to a phrase, separate multiple applicable tags in other variables (e.g., commenter_agreement, commenter_conflict, pressure).

rubrics_metrics.name: commenter_agreement_phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Any text discussing agreement among commenters involving this commenter (used to identify dimensions of conflict).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paste or record the exact phrasing from the agency response that indicates agreement among commenters on issues relevant to this commenter.

rubrics_metrics.name: commenter_conflict_phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Any text discussing disagreement among commenters involving this commenter (used to identify dimensions of conflict).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record language that signals inter-commenter disagreement; separate multiple types if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: pressure_phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Any text the agency uses that references the scale or intensity of public engagement (e.g., number of comments) on the side of this commenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record phrases that the agency uses to signal pressure (e.g., references to volume, intensity, petitions). This variable is not mutually exclusive with commenter_agreement/conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: mutual_exclusivity note for response tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification that accept, compromise, concession, and reject are mutually exclusive classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a single phrase in agency response is coded into only one of these four categories. Other tags (e.g., commenter_agreement_phrases) may co-occur with response tags and should be separated with semicolons where multiple types apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: proposed_direction (rule-level regulatory stringency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code the proposed policy change's direction relative to the status quo on a 1–5 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale meanings: 1 = Proposed rule change rolls back regulation; 2 = Small overall deregulatory changes; 3 = No clear change in overall regulatory scope of stringency (e.g., qualitative change in funding criteria); 4 = Small overall increases in regulatory scope or stringency; 5 = Proposed rule change increases overall regulatory scope or stringency. See Judge‑Lord, McDermott and Cashore (2020) for more on defining regulatory stringency.

rubrics_metrics.name: final_direction (rule-level regulatory stringency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code the final rule result's direction relative to the status quo on a 1–5 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale meanings mirror proposed_direction: 1 = Rule rolls back regulation; 2 = Small overall deregulatory changes; 3 = No clear change in overall regulatory scope of stringency; 4 = Small overall increases; 5 = Rule increases overall regulatory scope or stringency.

rubrics_metrics.name: final_relative_direction (final relative to proposed rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code how the final rule compares to the proposed rule on a 1–5 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale meanings: 1 = Change rolled back regulation relative to the proposed rule; 2 = Small deregulatory changes from the proposed rule; 3 = No change; 4 = Small overall increases in regulatory scope or stringency from the proposed rule; 5 = Rule change increased regulatory scope or stringency relative to the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: coalitions (rule-level coalitions list and percent)
rubrics_metrics.description: List all coalitions identified in the rule separated by semicolons, with an estimated percent of all comments belonging to each coalition (including comments not in the org_comments sheet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format example: 'ACLU - 70%; AFP - 25%; AMA - 5%'. Provide estimated percent for each coalition; expect distributions to often be highly lopsided.

rubrics_metrics.name: issues (top topics of debate in the rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The top three topics of debate in the rulemaking; may include commenter asks that did not make it into the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the three dominant substantive issues in the rulemaking debate and record them. These are rule-level topical summaries derived from comments and agency materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: number_of_comments_received check (mass campaigns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the number_of_comments_received column matches the number of comments/signatures submitted for mass campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mismatch, correct it. For mass campaigns, ensure the sheet records the total signatures/comments; if agencies post one representative comment but others exist, do not penalize the campaign if other records are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: transparency coding for mass campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Code whether a mass campaign was transparent about its 'sponsor', 'signers', 'both', or 'neither'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency examples: explicit statement 'these are members of our organization' generally sufficient; a list of names with no contact info is not transparent. Sponsor providing phone number but not org name is insufficient. If research is required to find the org name, mark not transparent. If submitter uses a misleading org name to disguise sponsor, mark not transparent. Record transparency in the transparency column or notes if the sheet lacks that column.

rubrics_metrics.name: platform recording for mass campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the tech platform(s) used to generate comments (if present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common platform labels: 'VoterVoice', 'Care2', 'SalesForce'. If a platform column exists, use it; otherwise record platform info in notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: fraud indicators for mass campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Record any indication of fraud associated with a campaign (e.g., technical validation failures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the sheet has a fraud column, record indicators (e.g., 'DMARC validation failed'); if not, record evidence of fraud in notes. Examples include suspicious email/domain issues, obviously fake names, or other signs agencies or researchers flag.

rubrics_metrics.name: coalition and coalition_type coding (comment-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code coalition and coalition_type for comments when identifiable (especially for org, mass, and elected types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every mass comment must be assigned a coalition. For orgs and elected officials, code coalition if immediately obvious; for individuals code only if obvious. coalition_type should summarize the nature of the coalition (e.g., business coalition, public interest coalition). If multiple signatories imply a coalition, add '; coalition' to org_type as appropriate.
